previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, chills, nausea, and worsening abdominal pain, two days after discharge from a prior admission for chronic pancreatitis complicated by Klebsiella bacteremia. She presented with a swollen, erythematous left arm and was found to have clinical signs of cellulitis and possible bacteremia, though blood cultures remained negative. She was treated with IV vancomycin and ceftriaxone. A new PICC line was placed in the right arm for antibiotic administration. Imaging showed persistent thrombosis in the left axillary and brachial veins with recanalization of the subclavian vein. She was kept NPO initially for pancreatitis management, then advanced to oral intake as symptoms improved. Warfarin was restarted with enoxaparin bridging due to concerns about absorption during flares. Reiki therapy helped manage anxiety. She improved clinically, became afebrile, and was discharged home on a six-day course of IV antibiotics via OPAT, warfarin, and her baseline medications.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo female h/o chronic pancreatitis due to rare genetic 
disorder (CFTR mutation) known to come to ER many times per year 
for IV pain meds and IVF now presenting with symptoms of nausea, 
vomiting, abd pain, and inability to tolerate PO intake, 
difficult access, DVTs in upper extremities.
.
# Chronic pancreatitis:
Per patient and her history, these symptoms due to her chronic 
pancreatitis. Also similar symptoms to past presentations to 
hospital. Most recent discharge with these symptoms was last 
month on ___. Lipase normal and alk phos only mildly 
elevated which are also consistent with past presentations.  Pt 
has specific drug regimen which she takes while in the hospital 
and which is outlined on in letter she bring from her PCP. Due 
to typical nature of this presentation no imaging has been done 
and is not warranted.  Pain and nausea were controlled with 
patient's typical regimen: Dilaudid 8mg IV Q2hrs (hang w/ 50cc 
bag NS and infuse over 15min), Toradol 15mg IV Q6hrs (hang w/ 
50cc bag NS and infuse over 15min), Zofran 4mg IV Q8hrs (hang w/ 
50cc bag NS and infuse over 15min), Phenergan 6.25 mg IV Q6hrs 
(hang w/ 50cc bag NS and infuse over 15min), and Ativan 0.5mg IV 
Q4hrs (hang w/ 50cc bag NS and infuse over 15min) and Ativan 1 
mg qhs.  On admission, patient's pain was ___ with a goal to 
get to ___.  She was kept NPO for the first 3 days of 
admission, then slowly began to advance her diet.  By Day 6, she 
was tolerating full POs without nauseaing and she was using her 
J tube to take formula.
.
#. Fever/Thrombophlebitis: On hospital Day #4, patient spiked a 
fever to 102 and her right peripheral IV site became 
erythematous, warm, and tender.  Patient was given 2 doses of IV 
vanco with relief of the erythema and fever.  Because patient 
remained afebrile, and was clinically improved, vancomycin was 
discontinued.  Right upper extremity ultrasound showed no clot 
at the vein site, however, did show a clot in her right IJ, most 
likely old.
.
# Left Upper extermity DVT/New DVT on right: Most recently noted 
in the left axillary and proximal brachial vein thrombus on U/S 
from ___ and also new found clot in right IJ thought to be 
old, as mentioned above. Patient had been on coumadin, which was 
held on admission due to poor PO intake and supertherapeutic 
INR.  Lovenox was begun when patient's INR was < 2.  Patient's 
coumadin was restarted on the day prior to discharge, and she 
was sent home with lovenox injections and instructions to have 
her INR checked at the end of the week.  Once INR was 
therpaeutic, she was instructed to stop the Lovenox.
.
# Hypertension:
Pt recently with increased problems controlling high BP in 
settings of abdominal pain and stressors. Had been started on 
10mg of lisinopril to help with BP but was not able to tolerate 
PO on admission. Admission BP elevated at 164/108, and remained 
140s-150s/90s.  Decision was made to administer IV metoprolol 
5mg Q6hr PRN for sys BP >180 and dia bp > 110.  Lisinopril was 
restarted upon discharge.
.
# Depression:
Chronic in nature. On a TCA as an outpatient. During most recent 
admission pt seemed very overwhelmed by the fact that her 
disease is ""becoming her life"". Received a trial of REIKI 
therapy by palliative care which brought brief symptomatic. On 
admission, will not be able to take amytriptiline as NPO. TCA 
was restarted upon discharge.
.
#. Access: Patient will be working with the IV nurses to get a 
port placed as an outpatient elective procedure due to need for 
frequent hospitalizations and poor peripheral access.
